name: Flood & Flash Flood
description: Comprehensive decision logic for rising floodwaters, urban waterlogging, flash surges, stranded residents, and contaminated utilities.

flood_start.prompt: What is your current location and setting regarding the flood situation?
flood_start.context: Flood response differs fundamentally whether you are inside a shelter, traveling on foot, or inside a vehicle.

options.text: Inside a house, apartment, or commercial building
options.description: You are sheltered inside a fixed structure.

options.text: Outdoors on foot (Road, alley, open terrain, or riverbank)
options.description: You are walking or stranded outside in rising water.

options.text: Inside a motor vehicle (Car, two-wheeler, or commercial transport)
options.description: You are traveling or stranded inside a vehicle on waterlogged roads.

flood_indoor_severity.prompt: How high has the water risen inside or around your building?
flood_indoor_severity.context: Water depth and rate of rise determine whether you should vertically evacuate to upper levels or signal for boat rescue.

options.text: Water is beginning to seep into the ground floor (Ankle deep / < 6 inches)
options.description: Inundation just starting; window of opportunity for utility isolation.

options.text: Water is rising rapidly (Knee-to-waist deep or fast flash surge)
Ground floor is submerged; stranded on upper floor or rooftop
options.description: Vertical evacuation already performed; awaiting external rescue.

flood_indoor_utility_check.prompt: Where is your main electrical distribution board located relative to the water?
flood_indoor_utility_check.context: Electrocution through water is one of the most common causes of indoor flood deaths.

options.text: Main breaker is high, dry, and safely accessible without standing in water
options.description: Safe to cut off electrical power and secure gas cylinders.

options.text: Water has reached the electrical panel or wiring is submerged
options.description: Touching electrical panels or walking in electrified water is lethal.

flood_indoor_rooftop_signaling.prompt: Are you on the open rooftop or trapped inside an enclosed attic / loft?
flood_indoor_rooftop_signaling.context: Attics without roof hatch access can become drowning traps if floodwaters reach the roofline.

options.text: On an open rooftop or balcony with unobstructed view of the sky
options.description: Visible to aerial search and boat rescue teams.

options.text: Trapped in an enclosed attic space with rising water below
options.description: Need to break onto the roof surface immediately.

flood_outdoor_severity.prompt: What are the characteristics of the outdoor water surrounding you?
flood_outdoor_severity.context: Moving water exerts immense hydrodynamic pressure. Just 15 cm (6 inches) can sweep a full-grown adult.

options.text: Water is actively flowing or has a noticeable current (even ankle-deep)
options.description: High risk of footing collapse, open manholes, and hydrodynamic sweep.

options.text: Stagnant / standing water blocking your pathway to high ground
options.description: Hidden open manholes, biohazards, and displaced reptiles.

flood_outdoor_hazards_check.prompt: Are there submerged drains, downed electric poles, or snakes/wildlife visible?
flood_outdoor_hazards_check.context: Displaced venomous snakes and energized urban stormwater present severe secondary risks.

options.text: Downed electrical cables nearby or dislodged manhole covers suspected
options.description: Extreme risk of electrocution or suction into stormwater drains.

options.text: No live wires; visible high ground or multi-story concrete structure nearby
options.description: Direct path to an elevated refuge.

flood_vehicle_severity.prompt: What is the vehicle's exact situation on the flooded roadway?
flood_vehicle_severity.context: Over half of all flood fatalities occur inside vehicles. 30 cm (12 inches) of water can float most passenger cars.

options.text: Driving towards a waterlogged or submerged section of the road
options.description: Water depth across the roadway ahead is unknown.

options.text: Vehicle has stalled / engine cut out in rising water
options.description: Water is accumulating around vehicle doors.

options.text: Vehicle is floating or actively being swept by current
options.description: Immediate vehicle sinking and rollover threat.

flood_vehicle_escape_check.prompt: Can you open the vehicle doors or are they jammed by water pressure?
flood_vehicle_escape_check.context: External water pressure against doors makes opening them physically impossible until pressure equalizes or window is breached.

options.text: Doors can still be opened; water is below door sills
options.description: Safe window to exit on foot towards high ground.

options.text: Doors cannot be opened due to outside water pressure
options.description: Need to escape through side windows immediately.

guidance.summary: Water is beginning to enter ground level. You have a brief window to de-energize circuits and move up.
immediate_actions: Stand on a dry wooden stool or rubber mat and switch off the main electrical breaker immediately.
Close the regulator knob on all LPG cylinders and move cylinders to an elevated platform if feasible.
Grab your pre-packed emergency 72-hour Go-Bag, medications, and vital documents in a waterproof pouch.
Move family members, children, and pets to the first floor or upper levels immediately.
Fill clean containers, bathtubs, or bottles with potable tap water before municipal supply is cut or contaminated.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT touch any electrical switches or appliances if standing in water or with wet hands.
DO NOT delay your move to upper levels to save heavy ground-floor furniture.
DO NOT attempt to drive your car out of the garage if the driveway is already submerged.
preventive_measures: Unplug all electrical appliances and move valuable electronics to higher shelves.
Monitor Central Water Commission (CWC) or local DDMA flood bulletin.
guidance.official_reference: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) — Management of Floods Guidelines & CWC Flood Protocol

guidance.summary: Water has contacted electrical fixtures. Standing in or touching this water carries severe risk of fatal electrocution.
immediate_actions: STAY COMPLETELY CLEAR of the submerged electrical panel and do NOT touch water connected to wall outlets.
Wade cautiously away from electrical panels toward higher dry surfaces, lifting your feet carefully.
Move upstairs immediately via interior dry stairs.
Call the local electric utility company or 112 from a dry mobile phone to request immediate neighborhood power line tripping.
Warn everyone in the house loudly to stay out of the ground floor water.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT try to reach the breaker box through standing water — even a tiny current can paralyze muscles and cause drowning.
DO NOT plug or unplug any corded electronics.
DO NOT use corded landline phones.
preventive_measures: Assume all floodwaters in residential areas are electrically charged until utility transformers are confirmed shut down.
guidance.official_reference: Central Electricity Authority Safety Directives & NDMA Flood Safety Protocols

guidance.summary: Rapidly rising water or flash flood surge detected. Move immediately to the highest accessible level.
immediate_actions: Move all occupants upstairs or to the rooftop immediately without pausing to pack belongings.
Take your mobile phone, charger, power bank, whistle, and any prescription medications if in your pocket.
Carry a bright flashlight or torch to signal rescue teams at night.
Once on an upper floor, secure the door against the stairs if it can slow water entry, but keep rooftop access open.
Call 112 or NDRF at 1078 to log your exact GPS location, building landmark, and number of trapped persons.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT go outside into the street — fast currents can knock you over or drag you into storm drains.
DO NOT hide in a closed basement or ground-floor bathroom.
DO NOT drink floodwater under any circumstances; it contains untreated sewage, chemical runoff, and pathogen bacteria.
preventive_measures: Conserve phone battery by switching to battery saver and using text messages instead of voice calls.
guidance.official_reference: NDMA Standard Operating Procedure for Flash Flood Evacuation

guidance.summary: Stranded on open rooftop awaiting boat or helicopter rescue. Make your position clearly visible.
immediate_actions: Tie a brightly colored bedsheet, cloth, or flag (white, orange, or red) to a flagpole, pole, or rooftop water tank.
Blow a whistle in bursts of 3 short blasts when you hear boats, drones, or helicopters.
At night, use a flashlight or smartphone screen to flash rhythmic light beams toward rescue personnel.
Keep small children, elderly, and pets away from slippery rooftop edges.
Cover yourselves with tarpaulin, umbrellas, or blankets to prevent hypothermia from prolonged rain exposure.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT attempt to swim across the flooded neighborhood to reach other buildings.
DO NOT climb onto frail tin sheds, asbestos sheets, or decorative parapets that cannot bear weight.
DO NOT attempt to board rescue boats by jumping into them; wait for rescue personnel to secure the boat.
preventive_measures: Ration available drinking water and dry food supplies carefully.
Boil any water obtained from rain before drinking.

emergency_contacts.name: Indian Coast Guard / Navy Maritime Rescue

guidance.official_reference: NDRF Inundation Rescue Protocols & NDMA Flood Guidelines

guidance.summary: Rising water inside an enclosed attic space can cause drowning unless a hole is breached to the outer roof.
immediate_actions: DO NOT remain enclosed in an attic with rising floodwaters if there is no pre-existing roof exit hatch.
Use a crowbar, axe, hammer, or heavy tool to break through roof tiles/shingles to get OUT onto the exterior roof surface.
Signal loudly from the open exterior roof once you emerge.
Pull everyone onto the roof and secure yourselves together with ropes or belts.
actions_to_avoid: NEVER climb into a closed attic space that does not have an exterior roof hatch or tools to break out.
DO NOT wait until water is at chest height to attempt breaking the roof structure.
preventive_measures: Once on the roof surface, signal with high-visibility fabrics.

guidance.status: IMMEDIATE RULE: NEVER CROSS MOVING FLOODWATERS
guidance.summary: Moving water is deceptive and forceful. Just 15 cm (6 inches) of rapid current will sweep you off your feet.
immediate_actions: TURN AROUND IMMEDIATELY. Do not step into or attempt to cross the flowing water channel.
Retreat along dry ground towards the nearest elevated building, masonry wall, or higher terrain.
If water is rising all around you and you cannot retreat, climb the nearest sturdy, permanent structure (concrete building, reinforced stairs).
If swept by current: Roll onto your back with feet pointed downstream to absorb impacts with rocks/debris, and angle yourself toward the shore.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT walk, wade, or swim across moving floodwaters under ANY circumstances.
DO NOT walk along canal banks, river embankments, or drainage culverts which can collapse without warning.
DO NOT touch wet metal railings or light poles which may be energized.
preventive_measures: Always carry a walking stick or pole to probe ground depth and stability if forced to walk through murky, still water.
guidance.official_reference: NDMA Flood Safety Protocol & CWC Flood Warning Guidelines

guidance.summary: Submerged streets hide open manholes with powerful hydraulic suction, and fallen cables energize the water.
immediate_actions: Stop immediately and maintain at least 10 meters distance from any fallen wire or transformer.
If you feel tingling in your legs or water, jump on one foot or shuffle feet closely together away from the area.
Look for swirling whirlpools or vortexes in the water — these indicate missing manhole covers with deadly suction.
Use a stick to test every step ahead of you before putting full weight down.
Climb onto elevated sidewalks, shop verandahs, or building porticos.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT walk through turbid floodwaters without probing depth with a stick.
DO NOT touch any metal utility pole, signpost, or fence in flooded areas.
DO NOT allow children to play, splash, or swim in floodwater.
preventive_measures: Report displaced manhole covers and downed wires to municipal disaster control rooms immediately.

guidance.summary: Path to high ground is visible and free of live wires. Evacuate immediately before water depth increases.
immediate_actions: Walk deliberately towards the elevated terrain or multi-story public shelter (school, temple, community hall).
Use a stick to probe for uneven ground, open gutters, or debris under the water surface.
Stay together in a group; hold hands or use a tether rope if moving with children or elderly persons.
Once on high ground, wash hands and legs with clean bottled water and soap as soon as possible to remove floodwater pathogens.
Check feet for cuts or punctures and apply antiseptic immediately.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT wade through floodwaters with bare feet; wear sturdy gumboots or closed footwear.
DO NOT consume fruits, vegetables, or food items that have come in contact with floodwater.
preventive_measures: Report to the nearest local relief camp organized by the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA).

guidance.status: MOTORIST SAFETY: TURN AROUND, DON'T DROWN
guidance.summary: Approaching waterlogged roadway. Never drive through flooded roads regardless of vehicle size.
immediate_actions: TURN AROUND IMMEDIATELY and take an alternate, elevated route.
If an alternate route is not available, pull over safely on elevated dry ground, engage the handbrake, and wait.
Recognize that 30 cm (12 inches) of moving water can float a car, and 60 cm (24 inches) will sweep away trucks and SUVs.
The road underneath may be washed away, leaving a hidden chasm or sinkhole under the water.
Warn following vehicles by turning on hazard flashers.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT attempt to drive through waterlogged roads, flooded underpasses, or submerged bridges.
DO NOT drive around barricades or road-closed warning signs set up by police.
DO NOT underestimate the force of moving water.
preventive_measures: Check live traffic and flood advisories on municipal or traffic police channels before commuting.
guidance.official_reference: NDMA Motorist Flood Safety Protocol & IRC Guidelines

guidance.summary: Vehicle stalled in rising water. You must exit immediately before water pressure jams doors shut.
immediate_actions: Unbuckle your seatbelt and unlock all car doors immediately.
Open the door and step out onto the roadway while water level is still below the door sill.
Abandon the vehicle and move quickly on foot to higher ground.
Help fellow passengers exit immediately, taking small children in arms.
Do not waste time trying to restart the engine or retrieve luggage; floodwater entering the exhaust/air intake has already seized the motor.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT stay inside a stalled car hoping the water will recede; vehicles easily become lethal floating traps.
DO NOT attempt to push the car out of the water.
DO NOT leave car keys behind in a locked door; leave vehicle unlocked for emergency towing.
preventive_measures: Once on safe high ground, notify 112 with your vehicle's location so other motorists do not collide with it.
guidance.official_reference: NDMA Standard Operating Procedure for Vehicle Flood Rescue

guidance.summary: Doors are jammed by outside water pressure. Escape through the side windows immediately.
immediate_actions: Roll down the electric power windows IMMEDIATELY before vehicle electronics short-circuit.
If electric windows fail, remove your car seat headrest and use its pointed metal prongs to smash the corner of a SIDE window.
Never try to smash the windshield; windshields are laminated safety glass and cannot be broken easily.
Push out glass fragments with your shoe and climb out through the window onto the roof of the car.
From the vehicle roof, assess water depth and current, and signal for rescue or leap to adjacent high structures.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT panic and waste energy kicking against locked, water-pressurized doors.
DO NOT attempt to break windows with your bare fist.
DO NOT jump blindly into deep, fast-flowing torrents.
preventive_measures: Keep an automotive emergency window-punch and seatbelt cutter in your vehicle's glovebox or center console.
guidance.official_reference: NDRF Vehicle Extraction Standard Operating Procedure

guidance.summary: Vehicle is floating or caught in flood current. The vehicle will quickly roll over or sink engine-first.
immediate_actions: SEATBELTS OFF: Immediately unbuckle everyone's seatbelts.
WINDOWS OPEN: Roll or kick out side windows before the car sinks below the water line.
CHILDREN FIRST: Push older children through the window onto the vehicle roof, then climb out yourself.
Get on the vehicle roof to maintain visibility for rescuers and stay above the water line as long as possible.
If the vehicle sinks completely, take a deep breath as water equalizes at roof level, open the door, and swim to the surface.
actions_to_avoid: DO NOT try to save luggage, laptops, or belongings.
DO NOT stay in the car seat expecting air pockets to last; water fills cabins in less than 60-90 seconds.
preventive_measures: When swimming away from a sinking car, swim with the current at a diagonal angle towards riverbanks or trees.
